answer: The cheapest real defence: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because bridge only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any willow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
